reporting-org.narrative: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

description.narrative: Provision of a sovereign loan of up to USD 19 million (EUR 17.1 million) to the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan to finance the construction of a new, modern, and efficient wastewater treatment plant in West Irbid to serve the wastewater networks being constructed under another EBRD-financed project, "West Irbid Wastewater Network Project". Collectively both projects will establish an improved and sustainable wastewater system in the area of West-Irbid, providing wastewater connections and services to the surrounding towns for the first time and replacing the current wastewater effluent storage practices from cesspools to an advanced wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) with pre-treatment facilities; which will positively impact the livelihoods of the residents. Project will be co-financed by an investment grant of up to USD 8 million (EUR 7.2 million equivalent) from the UK government under EBRD's High Impact Partnership for Climate Action multi-donor fund ("HIPCA UK") and an investment grant of up to the USD equivalent of EUR 2.75 million from the European Union Neighbourhood Investment Platform ("EU NIP"). In conjunction with the ongoing Wastewater Networks Project, the Project will introduce treated wastewater connections and services to the surrounding towns for the first time, replacing the current cesspool disposal system and thereby positively impacting the livelihood of the residents. The Project is anticipated to benefit approximately 200,000 individuals by 2045, depending upon the pace of project implementation. The existing Wadi Al Arab WWTP in West Irbid is nearing its capacity, necessitating urgent action to initiate the construction of the proposed Project to accommodate the additional effluent conveyed through the new sewage networks currently being constructed (50% completion) under the scope of the EBRD-financed West Irbid Wastewater Networks Project. The West Irbid WWTP will be positioned at a lower altitude relative to the sewage networks in the area of West Irbid, enabling gravity conveyance of the effluent rather than relying on energy-intensive pumping stations which will reduce energy consumption and operational costs The Project will also minimize the carbon footprint by replacing the current wastewater effluent storage practices from cesspools to an advanced wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) with pre-treatment facilities; which will positively impact the livelihoods of the residents. The Project will also contribute to Jordan's comprehensive wastewater investment program, offering effective solutions to existing sector challenges and creating employment opportunities for underserved groups. Simultaneously, it will promote the development of human resources and the implementation of policies fostering equality of opportunities within the Water Authority of Jordan.
